stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding the size of a skin prick test wheel?

options.text: The size indicates the likelihood of an allergy but does not predict the severity of a reaction.
A wheel larger than $10$ mm guarantees that the patient will experience anaphylaxis.
Smaller wheel sizes are only relevant for patients older than two years of age.
The wheel size must be measured exactly $60$ minutes after the prick for maximum accuracy.

explanation: Larger wheels correlate more strongly with a true clinical allergy, but they do not tell us if a reaction will be mild or anaphylactic.
rationale: Recall the distinction between the probability of reacting and the intensity of that reaction.

optionExplanations.A: Larger wheels correlate more strongly with a true clinical allergy, but they do not tell us if a reaction will be mild or anaphylactic.
optionExplanations.B: Size cannot determine the physiological severity of a potential future reaction.
optionExplanations.C: Wheel size interpretation is relevant for all ages, though different cut-offs are used for children under two.
optionExplanations.D: Skin prick tests are read much sooner, typically between $15$ to $20$ minutes after application.
